meta.title: Fae Club, the plan
meta.desc: The plan behind the new Fae Club site, one checkout with pay in 3 and the QR ticket the moment it's paid. Prepared by Astra, October 2026.

cover.by: Prepared by Astra for Elle Lawrence, October 2026
cover.h: One checkout for every Fae Club ticket.
cover.lede: Pay in full or in 3 in the same place, and the QR ticket lands the moment it's paid. Here's what we'd change, why it's worth doing while the Fairytale Ball is selling, and the first 90 days.

found.t: Pay in 3 tickets are sold as a second copy in the shop, and each guest is RSVP'd by hand before their QR goes out.
found.src: Your Enchanted, Royal and Night Club shop pages

found.t: The pay in 3 link at the top of Upcoming Events opens a page that says “This product couldn't be found”.
The Fairytale Ball is 66% sold with 174 days to go. The tickets sell, it's the paying that takes the work.

today.h: Your own pages say where the time goes.
today.quote: In order to make more payment options available to our community we had to set up these orders in a different way which can cause a delay in processing time as we will need to manually RSVP each guest.
today.quote_src: Every pay in 3 ticket in your shop, and the Night Club ticket, 25 Oct 2026
today.lede: Two checkouts sell one ticket. The event checkout takes the full price. The shop sells a copy of the same ticket so people can pay in 3, and that copy needs you to add each guest by hand before their QR is emailed, within 48 hours.

price.lede: On 25 October, 66% of the Fairytale Ball was gone with 174 days to go, and the Lions Solstice sold out in under 48 hours. On the same night as your ball, the Eternal Throne Ball at Stowe House sells from £190 plus £38 VAT. Move the switch to see what a guest pays on the day they buy.

hours.h: What the hand work costs you.
hours.lede: Every shop order means adding a guest by hand and sending their QR. Only you know how many and how long, so set both. The numbers start as an example.
hours.src: An estimate you set. Nothing here comes from your sales.

built.h: The new site, built around one ticket.
built.lede: One order carries down the page. The guest picks who they'll be, reads the night in your own words, chooses a ticket and how to pay, and the checkout arrives filled in. The ticket is one tap away the whole time, with the price and a ticket button on the first screen, the order in a bar at the foot of the screen through the book, and the same button again at the end of the night.

shots.p: Your own question opens the site, under the moon and fairy from your logo. The answer gathers in her stardust as one of your guests in that look, then lands on the cover of the book and later on the ticket. The price and the ticket button sit right under it, for the guest who's already decided.

Scroll and the book opens, gilt edges, drop caps and arches like the Spanish Hall's. The Prosecco or elderflower fizz, the characters, the dances, the costume contest and the DJ, in your words and your photos.
The last page opens into your photo of the hall at the Winter Gardens, with your own line on it and the ticket button under it, at the moment they most want to go.

Enchanted and Royal (VIP) as two foil invitations that catch the light. Royal is closed with a wax seal, and sold out shows the same everywhere. Choosing Enchanted takes the guest straight on to how they'll pay.
One switch. Three arches fill with each payment's share, worked out to the penny from the ticket and the fee.
Pay, and the QR gathers from gold dust on a ticket with the guest's name, and a wax seal presses on. In the prototype nothing is charged or sent.

under.lede: We'd build the site and take payments through Stripe with Klarna switched on. Stripe offers Klarna to UK businesses and pays the business in full up front, while Klarna collects the instalments and covers unpaid credit.
items: One checkout
Pay in full and pay in 3 on the same page, for every event.
The QR ticket
The site makes it when the payment clears, shows it on screen and emails it. No RSVP by hand.
One count per tier
Each tier has one number of places. If you hold some back, that's a setting on the tier.
The door
A scanning page on any phone marks each ticket as used, so your team can check guests in.
Tickets already sold
Everyone who's bought for 17 April keeps their ticket, and their names move into the new guest list so the door can find them.
The dates
Klarna sets when each instalment is due. The dates in the prototype are an example.
under.alt: If you'd rather keep your site and change only the checkout, Ticket Tailor takes Klarna through Stripe as well. We'd still pick the new site, because then the balls and the retreat sell in one place.
under.src: stripe.com/payments/klarna and help.tickettailor.com article 8826630, updated 14 Jul 2026, both read 25 Oct 2026.

retreat.lede: Today the £1,795 Valkyrie Retreat is booked by enquiry, with payment plans arranged by email. On the new site a guest picks how many months, books with a friend for £150 off, and asks for her place with the plan already in it.
retreat.how: Stripe runs a plan like that as a schedule with a set number of payments, which ends by itself after the last one. You'd still confirm every place, as you do now.
